Approximately 50% of patients with UC have disease only 
involving the rectum. Damage to intestinal mucosa in UC
usually only involves the ﬁ rst two layers of tissue (mucosa and 
superﬁ cial submucosa) within the colon and rectum. But with
chronic disease, the intestinal wall can become so thin that the
mucosa is ulcerated. Th is is referred to as toxic megacolon. 
UC disease usually aﬀ ects one section of the gastrointestinal 
tract at a time, whereas Crohn’s disease often presents with a 
“skipping” pattern aﬀ ecting multiple portions of the gastroin-
testinal tract.
